segments.text: American Fork City Council — Budget Workshop — February 8–9, 2018:

entities.speaker: Robert E. Shelton
entities.remark-context: Police evidence storage and dispatch reliability

segments.text: Council Member Robert Shelton asked whether the Police Department’s requested storage shed would supplement existing storage and raised a dispatch-tower problem in which emergency communications were not reaching personnel. Chief Darren Falslev explained that the existing shed was full and contained a truck being retained as evidence in a murder case.

Police Chief Darren Falslev told the council that the department’s existing storage shed was full, in part because it contained a truck that had to be retained indefinitely as evidence in a murder case.

entities.label: Police staffing, evidence storage, dispatch, radios, and fleet planning

segments.text: The workshop documented an evidence-storage shortage, unreliable dispatch communications, staffing needs, and multiyear radio and vehicle planning. These matters bear on the department’s capacity to preserve evidence, answer calls, and equip personnel.
Relevant passages from the official meeting minutes:

Council Member Shelton noted the Police Department was also requesting a storage shed and asked if this would be in addition to what they have. Police Chief Falslev answered the current shed was already full. Chief Falslev explained that the current shed was housing a truck that had to be kept for an unknown amount of time as it was part of a murder case.

Council Member Shelton had a fourth big idea to add, which was the tower capacity with Dispatch. They needed to keep pressure on Dispatch to correct the problem of dispatching out emergency personnel and the communication not getting to the personnel.

Police
• Additional Personnel – there was a lot of growth that would be coming, but they do not have the personnel to handle the additional load. They need one additional records information specialist, a code enforcement officer, and traffic enforcement officer. They needed to dig out of the hole they have been in for years.
• Radio Switchover – they were able to upgrade radios to the first standard, so they were compliant for ten years to give them time to switch over to the second standard. They need to transition radios for a cost of $212,810 over five years.
• Vehicle Rotation Plan – they started a five-year rotation plan to replace vehicles; they need to capitalize on the investments to reduce repair and replacement costs. They would replace the radio when they replace the car.
